summary.one_liner: A curated set of single-file, dependency-free Python scripts that implement modern AI algorithms (GPT, LSTM, diffusion, DPO, MCTS and more) from scratch as readable, runnable programs.
summary.what_it_does: The repository holds about 54 standalone Python scripts organized into four tiers: Foundations (17), Alignment & Training (13), Systems & Inference (19), and Agents & Planning (5). Each script is self-contained and uses only the Python standard library, so it runs with a plain python command. Most scripts train a model from scratch and then use it for inference or generation, while some compare alternative variants side by side, and a few run untrained forward passes or non-learning algorithms. The README says the scripts are meant to finish on a laptop CPU and that 23 of them download makemore's names.txt on first run. The README also describes animated Manim visualizations (in a separate repo, with videos in Releases), a challenge set, and Anki flashcard generators.
use_cases: learn how GPT or attention works by reading minimal code
study LoRA, QLoRA, DPO or PPO fine-tuning without a framework
compare optimizers like SGD, Momentum and Adam
understand KV-cache, quantization or Flash Attention internals
prototype algorithms without PyTorch or TensorFlow
prepare for ML interviews with code-level explanations
notable: Each script is a single file with no local imports and no requirements.txt, and CONTRIBUTING.md forbids adding one
Scripts are tagged by recorded teaching kind (comparison, train_infer, forward_pass, algorithm_demo) in docs/catalog.json
Covers the full stack from tokenizers and GPT through alignment (DPO, GRPO), systems (PagedAttention, RoPE) and agents (MCTS, ReAct)
Includes evaluation statistics scripts such as error bars for eval scores and paired comparison of models
caveats: Targets readers already comfortable with Python and basic ML concepts; the README says it is not a beginner introduction
Scripts are educational reference implementations, not replacements for PyTorch or TensorFlow, and the README does not claim paper-scale results
23 scripts need network access on first run to download names.txt
Timing figures in tier READMEs are historical measurements from when each script was added
keywords: run ml code on laptop cpu
